stance.label: Short-term bearish, bounce meets a break-even wall; long-term in the bottom zone

headline: This bounce has little room: 3% higher sit 600K BTC of underwater short-term holder coins, and the buying came from perps while spot stayed away.
summary: Short-term bearish: Sunday's bounce was bought with perpetuals, funding turned positive, spot and ETFs did not follow, and 600K BTC of underwater short-term holder coins sit overhead at $62,000–$64,000. Long-term bullish: capitulation is large enough to push realized cap down 1.5% in 30 days, with valuation in the historical bottom zone. A close above $64,000 would show someone absorbing the break-even supply; a close below $58,525 is a new cycle low.

watch.label: 200-day MA
watch.note: 11 straight closes below; the close needs +18.2% to get back above

overview.lead: Both weekend closes held above $60K on shrinking volume; tonight's US stock open is the first time real money tests this low.
points: Close $61,170; the intraday low of $58,650 stopped $125 above the prior low of $58,525.
Volume was 0.75x the 20-day average and half of Saturday's; Fear & Greed 11, day 10 of extreme fear.
November to date −21.0%; the worst November since 2013 was 2018 at −37.0%.
Nothing new on the exit framework or the market stage; the close has been below the 200-day MA for 11 days.

cycle.lead: Valuation is now nearly as cheap as late June, and not one trend light has improved; the long-term case rests on valuation, with trend yet to join.
points: MVRV Z 0.22 and NUPL 0.115 are both 144-day lows; at the Jun 30 low they were 0.18 and 0.093 (CoinMetrics, Nov 21).
Relative unrealized profit is 33.5%, day 9 under our 35% floor line; only 8.7% of days since 2012 sat below that line (Bitview).
The market stage is still bull; the close has been under a falling 200-day MA for 4 days and the rule needs 30 to exit. Of 6 supporting lights only exchange supply is on.
Long-term holder supply in loss is 45.4%, down from 46.5% on Nov 20; Tidemark's bottom signal is 44.5, short of 50, and its cycle-low test runs to Dec 19.

market.lead: The down leg is not over: price is up just 4% from the low and needs a close back at $67,627 to turn the leg, with this cycle's densest traded zone in between.
points: The leg has run 62 days from Sep 21, −29.4% on closes and −32.1% at its deepest on Nov 20; larger than 92% of this cycle's 12 down legs.
The close sits −1.53 standard deviations in the short-term holder cost bands, with −1 at $66,233 (Bitview); only 3.3% of the past year's closes were lower than today's.
The Sell Pressure Index has been at 100 for 13 days with momentum at 0.09; this combination has occurred 20 times since 2012, with 12 gains after 90 days and a median further dip of 12% before exit.
The volume point of control is $63,750, on top of the thick $62,000–$64,000 supply; coins within ±5% of price are 9.0% of supply, mid-range since 2018 and not crowded.

deriv.lead: Leverage came back faster than spot: perps flipped to longs paying, retail long accounts thinned out, and option protection got only a little cheaper.
points: The buyer in today's first finding is here: perps on three venues were net taker buyers of 10,662 BTC on the day, with $55.1M of shorts and $21.2M of longs liquidated (Coinalyze).
Weighted funding is 1.41%, pulled up by Hyperliquid at 10.95%; on Binance (−1.08%) and Bybit (−0.45%) shorts still pay.
DVOL 55.4 versus 58.0 a day earlier; 7-day implied vol is still 8.3 points above 90-day and the 25-delta risk reversal is −9.6, so puts remain pricier than calls (Deribit).

The estimated liquidation bands are heavier above: 32K BTC of shorts at $65.0–67.8K versus about 9K BTC of longs at $53.7–55.1K (several exchanges, estimated). The book shows $236M of asks at $61,000 and $171M of bids at $60,000, both on Hyperliquid perps.

flows.lead: No new ETF numbers over the weekend, and the on-chain and stablecoin ledgers are both still draining; Asia is the only place paying up.
points: Realized cap, the subject of today's second finding, points the same way as stablecoins: supply is $282.5B, down 1.6% in 7 days and $18.6B in 30 (DefiLlama).
USDT trades at $0.9983 and its 7-day average discount widened to 0.153%, in the deepest 0.5% of readings since October 2022; holders are converting stablecoins back to dollars.
Coinbase spot shows 3,764 BTC of net taker selling over 7 days, less than the prior day's 5,878 and still at the low end since August 2021; the Coinbase premium net of the USDT discount is −0.005%.

The Korea premium is 2.0% and the Asian OTC USDT premium 0.95%. Apparent demand of −737K BTC lands on the echo date of last year's Nov 22–23 wallet move, a mechanical effect, so we do not read it as weaker demand yet.

onchain.lead: Peak capitulation has passed and the handover has not: coins keep moving from long-term holders to short-term holders, and about 89% of short-term holder supply is underwater.
points: The $62,000–$64,000 zone in today's first finding is where that supply is thickest; 636K BTC changed price level in 7 days and 88% of it moved at a loss (Bitview; an on-chain move is not always a sale).

Network-wide realized loss fell from $1.88B to $329M on the day (Bitview; Sunday volume is always light); short-term holders are on day 13 of concentrated capitulation, with intensity down from 4.03 to 2.57.

Long-term holders realized $3.88B of losses over 7 days versus $4.36B a day earlier, still above the Jun 30 episode; their 30-day net position is −158K BTC, negative for 110 days (bitcoin-data, Nov 21).

By address balance tier, addresses with 10K+ BTC added 71K BTC in 7 days and the 1K–10K tier shed 55K. Hashrate rose 18.4% on the week and the Nov 27 difficulty estimate is +9.1%; the close is just 2.8% above estimated production cost.

exit.lead: No new trigger, and every next condition is far away.
points: 11 straight closes below the 200-day MA at $72,326, 15.4% under it; the hedge buy-back condition was already met on Nov 17.
MVRV ÷ prior-cycle peak 0.407, with the 0.75 line at $110,783; the three top indicators read 6 / 6 / 37, all low (CoinMetrics, Nov 21).

news.title: BTC rallied again to $61,343 on Sunday, then gave back about a third; in that hour Binance perps were net buyers of 144.3M USDT against 15M in spot
news.read: Same direction as our data: on Coinalyze, Sunday's perps on three venues were net taker buyers of 10,662 BTC against 1,475 BTC in spot, and weighted funding flipped positive to 1.41%. The piece has Saturday's Binance spot sellers ahead by 201M USDT; our Coinbase 7-day figure is still 3,764 BTC of net selling. Leverage bought this bounce, and tonight's US stock open decides whether it holds; it does not change the cycle view.

news.title: JPMorgan: BTC production cost estimated at $86,000, with the gap above $26,000 after the break below $60K; miners may be adding to selling, ETF outflows were mostly retail, and the fall in stablecoin market cap shows capital leaving crypto
news.read: Its cost basis is far higher than ours: the close is 2.8% above our estimated production cost, and breakeven for a mainstream rig (20 J/TH at $0.06 power) is $67,427; the two methods are not netted against each other. The pressure points the same way: hashrate rose 18.4% on the week and the Nov 27 difficulty estimate is +9.1%, so miner costs are still climbing. The stablecoin outflow it cites is $18.6B over 30 days on our data.

news.title: Bearish posts outnumber bullish ones: Santiment's bullish-to-bearish comment ratio fell to 0.59 before recovering to 0.77; about 87% of the past day's liquidations were shorts (CoinGlass)
news.read: Our Fear & Greed reading is 11, day 10 of extreme fear; Coinalyze shows $55.1M of shorts and $21.2M of longs liquidated on Sunday, 72% shorts, same direction and the shares are not netted against each other. Extreme sentiment is a contrarian reference at best: of 16 drops into extreme fear since 2018, only 4 were followed by a gain after 30 days. It says sellers are tired; it does not say buyers have arrived.

news.title: Miner PowerCompute's lender sold 267 pledged BTC to repay nearly $22M of debt, and going-concern doubt remains; MARA sold 13,597 BTC, about $1.1B, in six weeks
news.read: A concrete case of miner selling. Our hashprice is $26.13 per PH per day, and the mainstream-rig breakeven of $67,427 is above the close; Hash Ribbons show no capitulation yet, and hashrate rose 18.4% on the week instead. The network mines about 452 BTC a day, so MARA's six weeks of sales equal roughly a month of issuance; this is supply-side pressure and does not change the cycle view.

news.title: Kraken's BTC/CAD briefly fell to C$24,250 (about $16,900) on Saturday, 71% below the dollar price at the time; Kraken says orders were processed correctly and trades stand
news.read: Our daily bars use Kraken BTC/USD, with a Saturday low of $55,100 and a Sunday low of $58,650, untouched by the CAD mispricing. What it shows is how thin weekend liquidity is: one pair losing its market maker was enough for a 71% dislocation. Yesterday we wrote that part of the 9.8% intraday range was a liquidity effect; this is supporting evidence.

news.title: Cross-chain protocol Chainflip lost about $12M to an attacker, including 122.86 BTC; it offered a 10% bounty with a deadline of Monday 13:38 ET
news.read: 122.86 BTC is about 27% of one day's issuance of 452 BTC, so it does not matter for supply; at the time of the report the coins were still at the attacker's second address. Our exchange supply is down 0.83% over 7 days (Nov 21), with no unusual inflow. An industry risk event that changes none of our reads.

news.title: CFTC chair: on-chain derivatives platforms face the same rules as traditional exchanges; Hyperliquid needs approval or a licensed venue to serve US retail
news.read: Hyperliquid shows up in several of our reads: the largest walls in the order book are on its perps, today's positive weighted funding comes from its 10.95%, and it holds about 16% of open interest across the five venues. The rules do not immediately change who can trade, so these reads are unaffected near term; longer term it depends on whether it reaches the US through a licensed channel. No change to the cycle view.

findings.title: First hurdle at $62–64K: underwater short-term coins wait, and perps did the buying
findings.lean_why: The thickest band overhead is all underwater short-term holders who may sell at break-even; leverage pushed price up while spot and ETFs did not follow.
findings.what: Price bounced and stopped right under a break-even wall: the $62,000–$64,000 band holds 600K BTC of short-term holder coins, and the close is within 3% of it (Bitview, Nov 22).
findings.why: This is the weekly structure analysis, and the question is who the bounce meets at $62–64K and who is there to absorb them. Start with who holds: short-term holders own 3.88M BTC at an average cost of $71,993, and about 89% of it is underwater at this close; the two thickest bands are 600K BTC at $62,000 and 500K at $64,000, and long-term holders have another 441K BTC in the $62,000 band (Bitview, Nov 22). Compare with a month ago: short-term holders hold 236K BTC more and long-term holders 222K less, so coins are flowing to short-term hands. In the last 7 days 636K BTC changed price level, and 557K of that had a cost above the 7-day high, meaning it moved at a loss; the largest arrivals were the $60,000, $58,000 and $64,000 bands (Bitview; an on-chain move is not always a sale). The estimated part: over 30 days the then short-term holders moved 1.29M BTC, most of it bought at $80,000–$84,000 (estimated; the total is 0.4% off the actual figure). Without any model, high-cost supply above $88,000 fell by 130K BTC in 30 days. Behavior matches the paper losses: STH-SOPR is 0.980, below 1 for 17 days, and the Nov 20 capitulation low of 0.963 was deeper than the Oct 30 one (CheckOnChain). Then who is buying: on Sunday perps on three venues were net taker buyers of 10,662 BTC against 1,475 BTC in spot on three venues; weighted funding flipped from −0.22% to 1.41%, with Hyperliquid at 10.95% annualized (Coinalyze). On the spot side, Coinbase still shows 3,764 BTC of net taker selling over 7 days and ETFs a $3.67B net outflow over 20 trading days (to Nov 20). Options stack up in the same zone: estimated dealer gamma is positive at $64,000, which tends to pin price there (Deribit, estimated).
findings.alt: The other path is that the wall gets absorbed: a close above $64,000 that holds means someone is taking the break-even supply, and $62–64K turns from resistance into support. Spot tells the two apart: Coinbase 7-day net taker flow turning positive and ETFs turning to net inflow are what it takes. Data limits: per-UTXO data with no entity clustering, so exchange wallet housekeeping counts as turnover; holders with paper losses do not always sell at break-even; positive funding is a one-day reading, and shorts still pay on Binance and Bybit.
findings.history: After short-term holders are broadly underwater, price is usually higher 30 days later, often after another leg down first. Short-term holder supply in loss has risen above 60% 16 times since 2015, with 12 gains after 30 days and a median of +8.4%; in 5 of them price first fell more than 10% within the 30 days, the deepest being −36% in January 2018 (Bitview). The price-near-thickest-band signal itself has no backtest.
findings.so: What changed is the room this bounce has: 3% higher it enters the most heavily traded zone of this leg, and without spot demand every step up meets someone waiting to get out even. What did not change is the long-term picture: sellers are taking losses at a rare scale and valuation is in the bottom zone. Yesterday we wrote that spot was not what bought the low back; today adds a detail, the buyer was perps paying to be long.
findings.next: By Nov 29: a close above $64,000 means the break-even supply was absorbed and this call is refuted; a close back below $60,000 means the bounce turned back at the wall.

findings.title: Capitulation is big enough to shrink realized cap: on-chain money down 1.5% in a month
findings.lean_why: Coins are changing hands below their cost, so the network's aggregate cost basis is shrinking; no new money is paying higher prices, which leaves a bounce short of fuel.
findings.what: The on-chain ledger went from flat to net outflow: realized cap is down 1.51% over 30 days versus +0.03% a week ago, the largest one-week deterioration of the past year (CoinMetrics, Nov 21).
findings.why: Realized cap sums every coin at the price it last moved, so it falls when sellers' losses exceed what new buyers pay up. Break down who is losing: short-term holders are on day 13 of concentrated capitulation, realizing 13,696 BTC of losses against 2,079 BTC of profit on the day (CheckOnChain, Nov 22); long-term holders realized $3.88B of losses over 7 days, 0.316% of market cap and still above the 0.292% at the Jun 30 low, while the LTH-SOPR 7-day average of 0.785 is the lowest since Jul 1 (Bitview). Network-wide net realized P&L totals −$10.5B over 7 days versus −$4.5B in the prior 7 (CoinMetrics). Other ledgers agree: stablecoins are down $18.6B in 30 days (DefiLlama) and ETFs show a $3.67B net outflow over 20 trading days. The 30-day cumulative net loss is 1.435% of market cap, right at the 1.438% trigger line for cycle-scale capitulation; that line may be blunter in the ETF era because ETF shares change hands on the stock market, off-chain. The one thing that disagrees is the daily size: network-wide realized loss fell from $1.88B to $329M (Bitview, Nov 22), so peak capitulation has probably passed while the 30-day sum keeps falling.
findings.alt: A shrinking realized cap is also something only bottoms produce: in March 2020 and June 2022 it fell fastest when capitulation was most violent. It measures how much sellers hurt, which is not quite the same as money leaving the way stablecoin redemptions are. The other path is that capitulation has peaked and the 30-day change stops within −2%, which would resemble June 2022, when price moved only 1.6% over the next 30 days. Data limits: CoinMetrics derives it from market cap ÷ MVRV with a one-day lag; it is per-UTXO, so exchange wallet housekeeping also moves realized cap; and Sunday's realized loss is always on the low side.
findings.history: A drop this fast in realized cap has had no consistent follow-through a month later. It has happened only 5 times since 2019, with 3 gains and 2 losses after 30 days and a median of +1.6%, about the same as +2.4% for any day; the worst was −16.3% after March 2020 and the best +51.1% after February 2024.
findings.so: What changed is the read on the money backdrop: the 30-day change in realized cap has been at or below zero since Nov 13, 9 days now, and it is accelerating, which is also why the capital-inflow light among the stage's supporting evidence is off. What did not change is its role: the money backdrop is not wired to the market stage or the exit framework. The second Nov 20 finding tracks stablecoins and ETFs; this one adds the on-chain ledger, and all three point the same way.
findings.next: By Nov 29: the 30-day change in realized cap back within −1% means capitulation is fading and the outflow slowing, which refutes this; below −2.5% means on-chain money is still leaving faster.

research.summary: No new Glassnode issue (the latest are the Nov 18 methodology piece and the Nov 17 Week On-chain; Market Pulse Week 48 is not on the list yet). New is JPMorgan's Nov 18 report (via The Block, Nov 20): ETF outflows were mostly retail and the drop in stablecoin market cap is capital leaving, in line with our read that buyers have not returned.

items.title: JPMorgan says bitcoin price correction widens gap to estimated $86,000 production cost
items.points: Original not read; the following is from The Block's account: central production cost estimate of $86,000, with BTC near $65,000 when the report came out; miners are likely adding to selling, and the gap narrows only as hashrate falls and difficulty adjusts down; October–November outflows from spot BTC and ETH ETFs resemble May–June and were mostly retail, while CME positioning fell only modestly; the decline in stablecoin market cap shows some capital has left crypto.
items.meaning: We see miner pressure in the same direction with the opposite timing: hashrate rose 18.4% on the week and the Nov 27 difficulty estimate is +9.1%, with no sign of miners exiting yet. Stablecoins are down $18.6B in 30 days, consistent with its read. Secondhand only, and its cost method differs from ours.

items.title: QCP market note (cited in: Bitcoin rises 9% from two-year low, reclaiming $60,000 as forced selling eases)
items.points: Original not read; the following is from CoinDesk's account: BTC's next meaningful recovery needs tech stocks to stabilize, rate volatility to fall and institutional flows to return; until then, rallies driven by short covering may struggle to turn into sustained upside.
items.meaning: Sunday's bounce was exactly that kind: pushed by perp buying and short covering. The three conditions get their first answer after tonight's US stock open; DVOL at 55.4 is only slightly off its high and ETFs show $3.67B of net outflow over 20 trading days.

items.title: Institutional Holdings of Bitcoin ETPs Reach New All-Time High
items.points: 13F filers added the equivalent of 49,229 BTC in Q3 and hold a record 356,491 BTC ($29.78B), 27.6% of spot BTC funds; advisers and wealth platforms are 40.5% of that after 9 straight quarters of net buying, while hedge funds fell from 50.6% at end-2024 to 19.0%. Since quarter-end, fund holdings fell 38,531 BTC through Nov 16.
items.meaning: Holders shifted from hedge funds to wealth clients, who entered around $80K. Our estimated ETF holder cost is above the close: the close is 22.5% below it and has been underwater for 12 days; methods differ, so the numbers are not netted against each other.

items.title: CryptoQuant says bitcoin is back in a bearish phase but has reached a 'value zone'
items.points: The original report would not open (403); the following is from The Block's account: BTC is below the 200-day MA at $72,900 and the 365-day MA at $75,900; 30-day demand growth is below −400K BTC, the fastest contraction since Jul 1; Bull Score 10/100; trader unrealized loss of −20% is a 'value zone', but such bottoms usually take at least two months; a sustained break of $62,000–$65,000 would weaken the zone.
items.meaning: Its $62,000–$65,000 has turned from support into overhead supply, the wall in today's first finding. 'Cheap but needs time' matches our read: the Dawn Index is in deep night and the weekly bull-bear score is negative.

items.title: Wall Street Bought at $80,000. What Now?
items.points: ETFs took in $6.36B in Q3 at a flow-weighted entry near $78,300; Q4 through Nov 17 shows $3.09B of outflow. Acceptance below $61,300 with ETF outflows above $300M a day points to the Jul 1 low of $57,803; three straight days of ETF inflow and STH-SOPR back at 1 are needed before $69,400 and $72,700.
items.meaning: We see none of its strengthening conditions: ETFs are still in outflow and STH-SOPR is 0.980, below 1 for 17 days. The close of $61,170 sits right beside its $61,300.

items.title: The Week On-chain: Capitulation Meets Support
items.points: BTC fell to $62K on Nov 15 with realized losses at levels seen only near the 2018, 2020 and 2022 lows; $62–66K holds about a fifth of short-term holder supply; the remaining long-liquidation band is $59.5–62.2K; reclaiming $74.1K would look like a base, while a daily close below $62K points to $58.5K and the realized price at $53.7K.
items.meaning: The $62–66K short-term supply it describes is 1.10M BTC in our $62,000 and $64,000 bands on Bitview, all of it underwater now and the first break-even supply on any bounce. Our realized price is $53,199.

items.title: No gain, plenty of pain
items.points: Paywalled, preview only: BTC has fallen below its 200-week MA, ETF exposure is back to mid-August levels and funding is negative; it argues these indicators have coincided with BTC bottoms before.
items.meaning: Funding has now flipped positive to 1.41%, removing one of its three bottom markers; the 7-day average of 2.25% is still in the lowest 20% of readings since 2021. Nothing newer is on its list.

items.title: BTC Market Pulse: Week 47
items.points: BTC fell about 13% on the week; futures open interest dropped 7.2% to $34.2B, the lowest since August; 25-delta skew 13.7%; ETF outflows of $995M on the week; its conclusion is that leverage was flushed and the market is less crowded.
items.meaning: A week later some leverage is back: our open interest is down just 0.5% over 7 days and flat over 30, while price fell 24.5% over the same 30 days. The next Market Pulse has not been published.

cards.dawn: Leaning bullish long term: heat has sunk into the Midnight bottom zone, where BTC was higher a year later 98% of the time; but the weekly score is negative for a 2nd week and flips bearish after 2 more.
cards.avgd: Bullish on value: distance below the nine cost lines ranks low in history and kept falling this week; past bear lows went near 5, and one drop under 10 still fell 46.6% further within a year.
cards.p20: Bullish: the top is far off. Price would need about 81% more, near $110,783, to reach the 0.75 line; Pi Cycle and the top radar sit low, and Tidemark leans toward the bottom side.
cards.lthloss: Leaning bullish, on the edge: the long-term holder loss share sits in the past bear-bottom range, below this cycle's 46.5% high; a close under about $58,500 sets a new high and breaks the bottom pattern.
cards.cyccmp: Neutral: this cycle is far shallower; past cycles were below −75% on the same day, and this one bottomed at −53.1%. Old bottom timetables don't transfer, though the long path still points up.
cards.levels: Bearish: price is below the true market mean and ETF buyers' cost, with a stack of cost lines at $72K–$74K overhead as breakeven supply; the next line below is the realized price at $53.2K.
cards.urpd: Leaning bearish short term: the thickest pile sits just above at 62–64K, where buyers get back to breakeven; this week's moved coins mostly moved at a loss. A close above 64K would mean it's absorbed.
cards.strike: Neutral: the year-end max pain sits well above price, and the pull toward it is weak evidence; the real walls are $60,000 puts and $80,000 calls, with negative gamma below amplifying any break.
cards.legs: Bearish: the down leg is not over and is already deeper than most past legs; it ends only on a close at $67,627, and candles still sit below the busiest volume price at $63,750.
cards.pullback: Bearish: three pullback lights have been on together for 23 days, and the 90-day median after that is still negative; selling pressure is maxed into a bottom combo, but two lights must go out to ease.
cards.profit: Leaning bullish, contrarian: nearly all short-term holders are underwater, and past moves above 60% saw a +8.4% median month; their cost near $72K means breakeven selling all the way up.
cards.sopr: Bearish: short-term holders have sold at a loss for nearly three weeks, this dip went deeper than the 10/30 one, and realized profit is a sliver of losses; SOPR back above 1 marks the handoff done.
cards.rpl: Bearish: the one-year ratio is in past cycles' bottom zone, but losses ran 8x profits over 7 days and the ratio sits at its low; historically lows held only after a rebound to 0.80.
cards.miners: Bearish: price is under the mainstream rig breakeven of $67,427 and difficulty is set to rise again; hashrate is still climbing with no capitulation, and a break of the $59,491 cost would force selling.
cards.etf: Bearish: this ETF outflow run equals about 21K BTC, 11.9x what miners mined in the same span; the 20-day sum is also in an outflow stretch and price is below Strategy's cost, so no institutional bid.
cards.pr-us: Neutral: net of the USDT discount, US demand matches offshore; most of the weak-looking premium is USDT trading under $1. Asia OTC carries a premium and perps are cheap, but US spot hasn't joined.
cards.ad: Bearish: new demand can't keep up with coins going dormant, with 30-day apparent demand at its lowest since 2020; realized cap stopped growing and stablecoins shrank 6.18% in a month. No new money yet.
cards.whale: Bearish: the 1K–10K BTC tier cut the most this week, and long-term holders have been net sellers for 110 days as coins flow to short-term hands; until the whales' 30-day turns positive, supply keeps coming.
cards.svd: Bearish: OKX spot takers still sell more than they buy, large orders are selling and only mid-size ones absorb; Coinbase spot is unusually heavy. A buyer-led 7 days would show spot joining the bounce.
cards.stk: Bearish: BTC has lagged the S&P 500, Nasdaq and gold for two months while still tracking Nasdaq closely; the 2-year yield sits above the Fed's upper bound and markets price a 93% hike. No tailwind from rates.
cards.fh: Neutral: funding is positive but low, so longs aren't crowded; yet open interest edged up while price fell 24.5% in a month, leverage built against the trend. Funding at 30% or below zero would give direction.
cards.vol: Neutral: implied vol is near a one-year high, above realized, and the front end is inverted: traders are paying for a big move. Options give size, not direction; watch whether 64K or 58.5K breaks first.
cards.oi: Leaning bearish: money is on the downside, with buyers' premium tilted to puts for 25 days and risk reversals favoring puts; the far-above year-end max pain has weak pull, so downside protection dominates.
cards.fng: Bearish: sentiment is in extreme fear, and past entries saw a −6.1% median over 30 days, worse than usual; retail attention hasn't spiked, and panic isn't worked off until the index is back above 25.
